sentences.en: But I think they're all part of the same tradition, which is what makes it so interesting.
sentences.zh: 但我认为他们都属于同一传统，正是这一点让它如此有趣。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: But obviously,
sentences.zh: 但显然，

sentences.en: it's much easier to kind of stress test the historicity of a saint in the 21st century or even the 16th century than it was in the Latin West amid the implosion of the Roman Empire.
sentences.zh: 在21世纪甚至是在16世纪去对一位圣徒的历史真实性进行压力测试，要比在罗马帝国崩溃之中的拉丁西方容易得多。

sentences.en: I mean, that's a real challenge.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，那才是一个真正的挑战。

sentences.en: So Galatius is pope in Rome at a time when the empire in the West has completely imploded.
sentences.zh: 所以格拉修斯在西方帝国彻底崩溃的时期担任罗马教宗。

sentences.en: And how do you work out what sources are reliable?
sentences.zh: 你该如何甄别哪些来源是可靠的呢？

sentences.en: I mean, it's absolutely telling that actually these opinions that are attributed to Galatius actually don't seem to have been written by him at all.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，最能说明问题的是，这些归功于格拉修斯的观点实际上似乎根本不是他本人写的。

sentences.en: They were probably, I think most scholars think, written by someone writing in Gaul about 50 years later.
sentences.zh: 大多数学者认为，它们很可能是大约五十年后由某个在高卢写作的人撰写的。

sentences.en: And it's a real problem because, of course, the church is all about the miraculous.
sentences.zh: 这是一个真正的问题，因为当然了，教会的核心就是奇迹。

sentences.en: I mean, at the heart of Christian teaching is the idea of something that is, by definition,
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，基督教教义的核心就是这样一种理念，它按定义来说，

sentences.en: supernatural and fantastical and not merely bounded by the limits of kind of earthly possibility.
sentences.zh: 是超自然的、奇幻的，并不单单局限于尘世可能性的边界之内。

sentences.en: But at the same time, you don't want things that might seem kind of so miraculous that they seem ridiculous.
sentences.zh: 但与此同时，你又不想让那些看起来显得过于奇迹以至于显得荒谬的东西存在。

sentences.en: It's hard to know whether to draw the line, Tom.
sentences.zh: 很难知道究竟该把界限划在哪里，汤姆。

sentences.en: Yeah, and I think the thing that's fascinating about George, maybe more than any other saint, is that he is the saint who, perhaps more than any other one,
sentences.zh: 是的，而且我认为关于乔治最令人着迷的地方，也许比任何其他圣徒都更甚，在于他这位圣徒，可能比其他任何人都更强烈地，

sentences.en: becomes a focus for stories that channel a very, very deep need that is kind of running deep in popular opinion.
sentences.zh: 成为了各种故事的焦点，这些故事引导了一种深植于大众民意深处的极其强烈的需求。

sentences.en: And for that very reason, perhaps, is kind of viewed with suspicion by the intellectual elites, you know, from the 5th century right the way up to the 21St.
sentences.zh: 也正因如此，从公元5世纪一直到21世纪，他或许在某种程度上一直备受知识精英的怀疑。

sentences.en: So let's get to it.
sentences.zh: 我们这就开始吧。

sentences.en: In that opening faith leader quote, the 3rd century, a Turkish Roman soldier joined a cult.
sentences.zh: 在开篇那位信仰领袖的引言中提到，公元3世纪时，一名土耳其罗马士兵加入了一个异教秘密团体。

sentences.en: Can we even get back as far as the 3rd century?
sentences.zh: 我们甚至能追溯到公元3世纪吗？

sentences.en: I mean, he may well have lived in the 3rd century, but if he did, the stories about him are first told 200 years later.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，他很可能生活在公元3世纪，但如果真是如此，关于他的故事直到200年后才首次被人讲述。

sentences.en: Or the sources, rather.
sentences.zh: 或者说，是相关记载。

sentences.en: Yeah, the huge problem is we have no sources that are contemporaneous with a George if he lived.
sentences.zh: 没错，最大的问题在于，如果确有其人，我们找不到任何与圣乔治同时代的文献记载。

sentences.en: And I think that that is something that, you know, Catholic writers in late antiquity are aware of and are wrestling.
sentences.zh: 我认为，这正是晚期古代的基督教作家们所意识并正在努力应对的问题。

sentences.en: But equally, I think the reason for George's popularity is that he's like a kind of lake into which all kinds of streams of popular stories flow.
sentences.zh: 但同样地，我认为圣乔治受欢迎的原因在于，他就像一个湖泊，各种民间故事的清流都汇聚于此。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And the first thing that he's a focus for isn't dragon slaying, but for having been a martyr.
sentences.zh: 他最早集中的焦点并非斩杀恶龙，而是他曾是一位殉道者。

sentences.en: And martyrs for Christians, you know, in the Roman world are the kind of the shock troops of the church.
sentences.zh: 对于罗马世界的基督徒来说，殉道者就是教会的突击力量。

sentences.en: They are the holieSt.
sentences.zh: 他们是最圣洁的人。

sentences.en: They are the people who don't have to wait around for the final judgment to get to heaven.
sentences.zh: 他们是不必等待最终审判就能进入天堂的人。

sentences.en: They go straight there.
sentences.zh: 他们直接就能去那里。

sentences.en: They're seated at the feasting table of God.
sentences.zh: 他们就坐在上帝的宴席旁。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So the stories that are told about George's martyrdom kind of take all the familiar elements and kind of crank them up to a massive pitch.
sentences.zh: 因此，关于圣乔治殉道的传说，吸收了所有熟悉的元素，并将其渲染到了极致。

sentences.en: So the stories that are told, and these are from the 5th century.
sentences.zh: 这些流传的故事可以追溯到公元5世纪。

sentences.en: So as you said, about 200 years after George is supposed to have lived.
sentences.zh: 正如你所说，大约是在圣乔治被认为生活的时期之后的200年。

sentences.en: They vary in the details, but you can kind of distinguish a basic outline.
sentences.zh: 它们的细节各有不同，但你还是能大致辨认出一个基本轮廓。

sentences.en: And what they say is that George is probably from Cappadocia, which is in the middle of what is now Turkey, but of course wasn't Turkey then.
sentences.zh: 它们记载的内容是，圣乔治可能来自卡帕多西亚，也就是现在土耳其的中部，当然那时还不叫土耳其。

sentences.en: So George was not a Turk.
sentences.zh: 所以圣乔治不是土耳其人。

sentences.en: There's no way George could have been a Turk.
sentences.zh: 圣乔治绝对不可能是土耳其人。

sentences.en: I mean, the Turks are like thousands of miles away on the steppes of Central Asia.
sentences.zh: 我是说，土耳其人远在数千英里之外的中亚大草原上。

sentences.en: Of course.
sentences.zh: 当然。

sentences.en: So George is a Greek.
sentences.zh: 所以圣乔治是个希腊人。

sentences.en: George is a Greek name.
sentences.zh: 乔治是一个希腊名字。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Gorgias.
sentences.zh: 高尔吉亚。

sentences.en: And there's kind of various traditions about where he was actually brought up.
sentences.zh: 关于他实际成长的地方，存在着各种不同的传统说法。

sentences.en: So there is a tradition that derives from a manuscript that was found quite recently when they were kind of shifting monuments to build the Aswan Dam.
sentences.zh: 有一种传统源自不久前在搬迁阿斯旺水坝纪念碑时偶然发现的一份手稿。

sentences.en: And in this, George grew up in Nubia.
sentences.zh: 在这份手稿中，圣乔治是在努比亚长大的。

sentences.en: But what the sources agree is that he rises very high in the imperial service, perhaps as a civil servant.
sentences.zh: 但各种文献一致认为，他在帝国体制中晋升极快，或许曾是一名文官。

sentences.en: But the general tradition, which becomes kind of canonical, is that he is a soldier, that he's a warrior fighting in the armies of Caesar.
sentences.zh: 不过，后来演变成经典正统的普遍说法是，他是一名士兵，是凯撒军队中征战的勇士。

sentences.en: So in one of the institutions, one of the great institutions of the empire, either way.
sentences.zh: 总之，不论哪种说法，他都属于帝国的伟大机构之一。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So it's either the civil service or the army, and he becomes associated with the army.
sentences.zh: 所以要么是文官系统，要么是军队，而他最终与军队联系在了一起。

sentences.en: He is baptized, and he is then ordered by a heathen emperor to sacrifice to Apollo.
sentences.zh: 他接受了洗礼，随后被一位异教皇帝命令向阿波罗献祭。

sentences.en: He refuses, and he then just suffers tortures that are so hideous that they kind of verge on the comical.
sentences.zh: 他拒绝了，接着便遭受了极其可怕的酷刑，简直有些滑稽可笑。

sentences.en: So in one version of the story of George, he is forced into shoes that have iron spikes inside them.
sentences.zh: 所以在关于圣乔治的一个版本中，他被强行穿上内部带有铁钉的鞋子。

sentences.en: He has his skull crushed.
sentences.zh: 他的头骨被砸碎。

sentences.en: He then has 60 nails hammered into it.
sentences.zh: 接着他的头上被钉入了60枚钉子。

sentences.en: And then just for good measure, he has molten lead poured down his throat.
sentences.zh: 为了保险起见，滚烫的铅水被直接灌进他的喉咙。

sentences.en: He's still alive at this point.
sentences.zh: 而此时他居然还活着。

sentences.en: He's then placed in a kind of giant hollow bronze bull, which again has kind of sharp nails inside it.
sentences.zh: 随后他被关进了一个巨大的中空青铜公牛里，同样，里面也布满了尖锐的铁钉。

sentences.en: And the bull is kind of revolved round and round so that these nails are kind of driving into him.
sentences.zh: 这头公牛被反复翻转，好让这些铁钉不断刺入他的体内。

sentences.en: Anyway, so all very horrible.
sentences.zh: 总之，过程极其恐怖。

sentences.en: And then in another account, he is broken on a wheel with knives, and this kills him.
sentences.zh: 在另一份记载中，他被绑在装有刀片的车轮上处决，这要了他的命。

sentences.en: He's restored to life by St. Michael, who we talked about in the previous episode, the captain of the angels who fights Satan in the great battle.
sentences.zh: 但他被我们在上一集讨论过的大天使长米迦勒复活了，就是那位在终极之战中与撒旦搏斗的天使长。

sentences.en: When he's restored to life, understandably, everyone in the heathen emperor's kingdom is very impressed by this.
sentences.zh: 当他复活时，可想而知，异教皇帝王国里的所有人都对此震惊不已。

sentences.en: And so they all mass conversions.
sentences.zh: 于是他们全都集体皈依了。

sentences.en: And the king is furious, continues trying to finish George off, so boils George alive, sores him in two, molten lead poured down his throat.
sentences.zh: 国王勃然大怒，继续试图处决圣乔治，于是将他活活煮沸、从中间锯成两半、并将熔化的铅水灌入他的喉咙。

sentences.en: And George is brought back to life by St. Michael three times in a row.
sentences.zh: 圣乔治就这样被大天使长米迦勒接连复活了三次。

sentences.en: And actually, if you win a martyr's crown, you go straight to heaven.
sentences.zh: 实际上，如果你赢得了殉道者的桂冠，你就能直升天堂。

sentences.en: You'd think George would be getting a bit frustrated by this.
sentences.zh: 你可能会觉得圣乔治对此开始感到有点沮丧了。

sentences.en: But he does finally win his martyr's crown on the fourth attempt, on the 23rd of April.
sentences.zh: 但他最终在第四次尝试时，于4月23日真正赢得了殉道者的桂冠。

sentences.en: And the entire kingdom is converted, except for the emperor, but his empress is converted.
sentences.zh: 整个王国都皈依了，除了皇帝本人，但他的皇后皈依了。

sentences.en: So the female members of the royal family are converted.
sentences.zh: 所以皇室的女性成员都皈依了。

sentences.en: Fair play to the emperor, though.
sentences.zh: 不过，也得夸夸这位皇帝。

sentences.en: I mean, he's sticking to his guns.
sentences.zh: 我是说，他够坚持。

sentences.en: He's sticking to his principles.
sentences.zh: 他坚守了自己的原则。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So basically, this is kind of, you know, this is the Marvel equivalent of a martyr.
sentences.zh: 所以基本上，这可以说是漫威版的殉道者。

sentences.en: This is pumping up all the stories about martyrdom to a kind of superhuman level.
sentences.zh: 这就好比把所有关于殉道的传说都夸大到了超人类的水平。

sentences.en: And I think that's why it's so popular.
sentences.zh: 我想这也是它如此受欢迎的原因。

sentences.en: And it's why, you know, intellectuals, clerical scholars are embarrassed about it.
sentences.zh: 这也是为什么知识分子和神职学者会对此感到尴尬。

sentences.en: It seems to them absurd and over-sensational and kind of threatening, because it makes the martyrdom narratives that are so important to the church just seem a bit far-fetched.
sentences.zh: 在他们看来，这荒谬绝伦、过分煽情且颇具威胁性，因为它让教会至关重要的殉道叙事显得有些牵强附会。

sentences.en: But also, it kind of complicates the way we think about these narratives, right?
sentences.zh: 但同时，这也让咱们看待这些叙事的方式变得复杂了，对吧？

sentences.en: We assume they're all one thing.
sentences.zh: 我们总以为它们都是千篇一律的。

sentences.en: But within the genre, there would perhaps have been as much diversity of quality as there was within, you know, any modern narrative.
sentences.zh: 但在这个类型内部，其质量的多样性或许就像任何现代叙事作品一样丰富。

sentences.en: In other words, there would have been stuff at the eyebrow end.
sentences.zh: 换句话说，其中也会有阳春白雪的高雅之作。

sentences.en: And this is very much a populist story, the sort of lowbrow, the Dan Brown of martyrdom narratives.
sentences.zh: 而这个故事绝对是个通俗故事，属于那种俗文化，堪称殉道叙事中的《达芬奇密码》。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: I think a kind of superhero film, perhaps, more.
sentences.zh: 我觉得它可能更类似于某种超级英雄电影。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 确实。

sentences.en: Because for some reason, George has become a figure who attracts these kind of stories.
sentences.zh: 因为出于某种原因，圣乔治成了一个吸引这类故事的标志性人物。

sentences.en: And the more he attracts the stories, the more he becomes the kind of the emblematic martyr.
sentences.zh: 而且他吸引的故事越多，他就越发成为那种具有象征意义的殉道者。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: All of which kind of the question hanging over this is, well, you know, did he actually exist?
sentences.zh: 所有这一切，悬而未决的问题其实是：他真的存在过吗？

sentences.en: And I think it's impossible to say.
sentences.zh: 我觉得这根本无法回答。

sentences.en: But is it not possible to say that a fantastical story like this, merely because it's become fantastical and the versions we have of fantastical,
sentences.zh: 但难道我们就不能说，像这样光怪陆离的故事，仅仅因为它变得光怪陆离，且我们见到的版本也都是魔幻色彩的，

sentences.en: does not mean there are no trace elements?
sentences.zh: 并不意味着其中就完全没有历史的痕迹吗？

sentences.en: Then the story must have begun somewhere.
sentences.zh: 那么这个故事总得有个起因吧。

sentences.en: Absolutely.
sentences.zh: 完全正确。

sentences.en: Either you believe somebody literally invented it from nowhere, or you believe there was a soldier who converted and that from that humble beginning,
sentences.zh: 要么你相信有人凭空捏造了这个故事，要么你相信确实曾有一位士兵皈依了信仰，而正是从这个卑微的起点，

sentences.en: a fantastical story was later created.
sentences.zh: 后人创作出了这样一个魔幻的故事。

sentences.en: I think so.
sentences.zh: 我也这么认为。

sentences.en: And it's kind of widely felt that the likeliest context for George, if he did exist, was the great persecution that's launched against the church by the Emperor Diocletian.
sentences.zh: 大家普遍认为，如果圣乔治真的存在过，最合理的背景便是由皇帝戴克里先对教会发起的残酷大迫害。

sentences.en: We did a whole episode about him for the World Cup, didn't we, a couple of years ago.
sentences.zh: 几年前世界杯期间，我们不是还专门为他做过一整期节目吗？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: He launches this basically to kind of extirpate the church at the beginning of the fourth century.
sentences.zh: 他在公元4世纪初发动这场迫害，基本上是为了根除教会。

sentences.en: And all the sources agree that George is being martyred for refusing to sacrifice to pagan gods.
sentences.zh: 所有的历史记载都一致认为，圣乔治是因为拒绝向异教神明献祭而殉道的。

sentences.en: And they also agree that this happens in the eastern half of the Mediterranean world, where the persecution was at its most brutal.
sentences.zh: 他们还一致认为，这件事发生在迫害最为残酷的地中海东部地区。

sentences.en: So I would say the likelihood is that he is someone possibly in the imperial service who is martyred in the early fourth century under Diocletian.
sentences.zh: 所以我想说，最大的可能性是，他可能是某个在帝国任职的人，于公元4世纪初在戴克里先统治时期殉道。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: I mean, even that is, you know, it's been disputed.
sentences.zh: 我是说，即便如此，这也是饱受争议的。

sentences.en: But I would say that's the likelieSt.
sentences.zh: 但我觉得这是最有可能的情况。

sentences.en: It's a reasonable best guess, right?
sentences.zh: 这是一个合理的最佳猜测，对吧？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So beyond that, kind of very difficult to know, because, of course, having a famous martyr is something that, I mean, it's a brilliant thing to have.
sentences.zh: 因此，除此之外的事情就很难知晓了，因为拥有一位著名的殉道者，这绝对是一件了不起的好事。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And so various places kind of compete over him.
sentences.zh: 所以各地都在争夺他。

sentences.en: So one favorite location for him is Lydda, which is modern day Lod, which is just south of Tel Aviv in Israel.
sentences.zh: 他最受青睐的一个归属地是卢德，也就是今天的洛德，位于以色列特拉维夫正南方。

sentences.en: His mother is supposed to have been the Komet who was in charge of the city.
sentences.zh: 据说他的母亲曾是管理该市的长官。

sentences.en: His relics were buried there.
sentences.zh: 他的遗物就被埋葬在那里。

sentences.en: I mean, if they really were his relics, we don't know.
sentences.zh: 我是说，那到底是不是他的遗物，我们也不得而知。

sentences.en: And Lydda undoubtedly becomes the kind of the main center for his cult in the Eastern Mediterranean.
sentences.zh: 毫无疑问，卢德后来成了他在地中海东部信仰崇拜的主要中心。

sentences.en: But it has to be said, again, that the evidence for this is quite late.
sentences.zh: 但必须再次说明的是，关于这一点的证据出现得相当晚。

sentences.en: And, you know, there are other places.
sentences.zh: 而且，还有其他一些地方。

sentences.en: So Joppa, Joppa, where the great skeleton of the sea monster was brought by Scouris.
sentences.zh: 比如约帕，也就是珀尔修斯带来海怪巨型骨骼的那个约帕。

sentences.en: Hey, maybe that sea monster, which was actually, what, a whale or something like that?
sentences.zh: 嘿，说不定那只海怪实际上是什么鲸鱼之类的大型海洋生物呢？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: How disappointing.
sentences.zh: 真让人失望。

sentences.en: So I was going to say, there's your St. George and the dragon.
sentences.zh: 所以我本来想说，这就是你们的圣乔治与恶龙的故事。

sentences.en: Oh, exactly.
sentences.zh: 哦，确实如此。

sentences.en: And Perseus rescues a princess from a sea monster there.
sentences.zh: 珀尔修斯就在那里从海怪手中解救了一位公主。

sentences.en: And that does seem to have echoes of the George theory.
sentences.zh: 这似乎确实与圣乔治的传说有着某种呼应。

sentences.en: But again, the problem with that is that these stories are much, much later.

sentences.en: And he has a list of kind of over 200 of these stories.
sentences.zh: 他列出了200多种类似的故事。

sentences.en: And the thing is, they're all remarkably similar.
sentences.zh: 关键是，它们都惊人地相似。

sentences.en: You know, they're kind of very conservative, the same pattern over and over again.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，它们非常保守，都是同样的模式一遍又一遍地出现。

sentences.en: But this is why George is interesting, because he is a warrior.
sentences.zh: 但这正是乔治有趣的地方，因为他是个武士。

sentences.en: He's a saint, but he is also a soldier.
sentences.zh: 他是个圣徒，但同时也是个士兵。

sentences.en: So Tom, just going back to that point and thinking about what you were talking about in our previous
sentences.zh: 所以汤姆，回到刚才那个点，想想你在我们上一期关于龙的历史的播客里谈到的内容，罗马世界的基督教作家，你知道的，没有人对他们说过，现在已经发生了巨大的文化转变。

sentences.en: podcast about the history of dragons, Christian writers in the Roman world, you know, no one has sort of said to them, there's been a massive cultural shift now.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道的，所以那些古典传说。

sentences.en: And, you know, so the classical legends.
sentences.zh: 那是他们精神世界的一部分。

sentences.en: It's part of their mental furniture.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 这完全是他们想象力的一部分。

sentences.en: It's totally part of their imagination.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，他们浸润在那个世界里。

sentences.en: I mean, they're steeped in that world.
sentences.zh: 他们完全沉浸其中。

sentences.en: They're completely immersed in it.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，很显然，如果认为他们不会讲那些融入了希腊和罗马神话元素的故事，那就太异想天开了。

sentences.en: I mean, obviously, it'd be fanciful to think that they wouldn't be telling stories that would be infused with elements of Greek and Roman mythology.
sentences.zh: 所以与怪物战斗以及诸如此类的事情。

sentences.en: So the fighting of the monsters and all that stuff.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我认为这没说错。

sentences.en: I mean, I think that's right.
sentences.zh: 话虽如此，当然，他们也意识到文化已经发生了转变，因为他们已经皈依了或者说他们已经重生了。

sentences.en: Having said that, of course, they are aware that there's been a cultural shift because they have converted or they have been born again.
sentences.zh: 是的，但用你的话说，他们并没有丢掉以前所有的精神家当。

sentences.en: Yeah, but they haven't dumped all their previous furniture, to use your expression.
sentences.zh: 不，绝对没有。

sentences.en: No, absolutely not.
sentences.zh: 但我想说的是，我认为对此有一个明显的基督教先例，那就是我们已经多次提到的圣米迦勒的形象。

sentences.en: But I'm just saying that I think that there is an obvious Christian antecedent for this, which is the figure of St. Michael, who we've mentioned quite a lot already.
sentences.zh: 天堂的统帅，英勇的大天使。

sentences.en: The captain of heaven, the warrior archangel.
sentences.zh: 一个与龙搏斗的人？

sentences.en: Who fights a dragon?
sentences.zh: 我认为这是一个显而易见的例子。

sentences.en: I think that's the kind of the obvious example.
sentences.zh: 而问题在于，因为他是个大天使，你知道的，他没有留下任何圣物。

sentences.en: And the issue with that is that because he's an archangel, you know, he hasn't left any relics.
sentences.zh: 他没有任何遗骨。

sentences.en: He doesn't have any bones.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 大天使没有骨头吗？

sentences.en: Do archangels not have bones?
sentences.zh: 那是怎么回事？

sentences.en: How does that work?
sentences.zh: 不，他们属于那种，不。

sentences.en: No, they're kind of, no.
sentences.zh: 他们是没有骨头的，就像拉姆齐·麦克唐纳一样。

sentences.en: They're boneless, like Ramsay MacDonald.
sentences.zh: 他们是没有肉身的。

sentences.en: They're incorporeal.
sentences.zh: 它们是没有实体形态的。

sentences.en: Right, okay.
sentences.zh: 对，好的。

sentences.en: So that's a source of frustration.
sentences.zh: 所以这令人沮丧。

sentences.en: Whereas with St. George, if you kind of, you model St. George on St. Michael, then you can have all the relics and it's kind of, he's more accessible, I guess.
sentences.zh: 而对于圣乔治来说，如果你把圣乔治当作圣米迦勒的模板，那么你就可以拥有所有的圣物，而且他会更平易近人，我想。

sentences.en: So I do think that St. Michael hovers behind these stories.
sentences.zh: 所以我确实认为圣米迦勒的影子笼罩在这些故事的背后。

sentences.en: But I agree that, of course, if you live in particularly the Greek speaking part of the
sentences.zh: 但我同意，当然，如果你住在特别是讲希腊语的

sentences.en: Roman Empire, of course, you're going to be familiar with all these stories.
sentences.zh: 罗马帝国，你当然会对所有这些故事耳熟能详。

sentences.en: And that's why perhaps the story of Perseus and Andromeda informs the stories about saints rescuing princesses or saving women or, you know, even young men, as in the example of
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么珀耳修斯和安德洛墨达的故事可能会为圣人拯救公主或拯救女性（甚至像圣托马斯那样的年轻男子）的故事提供背景。

sentences.en: St. Thomas.
sentences.zh: 圣托马斯。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: And that these then translate into the story of St. George.
sentences.zh: 然后这些故事演变成了圣乔治的故事。

sentences.en: Well, because just think about how it would work, right?
sentences.zh: 嗯，因为只要想想它是怎么运作的，对吧？

sentences.en: Imagine that you convert to Christianity when you're 20 or whatever.
sentences.zh: 想象一下你在20岁左右或其他什么时候皈依了基督教。

sentences.en: Presumably you're sitting there for the first, let's say, eight, 10 years of your life.
sentences.zh: 据推测，你在生活的前八年到十年里一直坐在那里。

sentences.en: I know that the stories are not children's stories in the same way that they are perceived as being children's stories today, the Greek myths.
sentences.zh: 我知道这些故事不像今天人们所认为的那样是儿童读物，我是指希腊神话。

sentences.en: But there's no doubt that you would be told a story about Perseus and Andromeda or Heracles and his labors or Theseus and, you know, the labyrinth and stuff.
sentences.zh: 但毫无疑问，你会听到关于珀耳修斯和安德洛墨达，或者赫拉克勒斯和他的劳作，或者忒修斯和迷宫之类的事情的故事。

sentences.en: I mean, of course you would.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，你当然会听到。

sentences.en: They're part of the common currency.
sentences.zh: 它们是通行货币的一部分。

sentences.en: It'd be as ubiquitous as the Beatles music is today.
sentences.zh: 它就像今天的披头士音乐一样无处不在。

sentences.en: So it would make sense that when you become a Christian or when you really get into Christianity,
sentences.zh: 所以这很合理，当你成为一名基督徒或者当你真正深入了解基督教时，

sentences.en: your sense of what is, you know, the frameworks for the stories you tell are dictated by not just the Bible, but also the other tradition that is there at the same time.
sentences.zh: 你对故事框架的感知不仅由圣经决定，还由同时存在的其他传统决定。

sentences.en: But I think that in the case of George, it's not like he's being modelled on the story of
sentences.zh: 但我认为就乔治而言，他并不是以

sentences.en: Perseus and Andromeda.
sentences.zh: 珀耳修斯和安德洛墨达的故事为模板的。

sentences.en: I think that the elements of those Greek myths of dragons that live in caves and, you know,
sentences.zh: 我认为希腊神话中那些住在洞穴里的巨龙以及英雄们与之搏斗的元素，

sentences.en: heroes fight them, that that has been kind of mediated and adapted by people who are writing stories of saints who confront dragons.
sentences.zh: 在某种程度上已经被那些撰写圣人对抗巨龙故事的人们所调和和改编了。

sentences.en: And then the massive innovation with George sometime around the 6th, 7th, 8th century is that he is a martial saint.
sentences.zh: 然后在6、7、8世纪左右，乔治带来了一个巨大的创新，那就是他是一位尚武的圣人。

sentences.en: He is a warrior saint.
sentences.zh: 他是一位武士圣人。

sentences.en: He's a soldier.
sentences.zh: 他是一名士兵。

sentences.en: And so then that just kind of lights the touch paper for reanimating all these kind of traditions and stories.
sentences.zh: 因此，这就像是点燃了引信，重新激活了所有这些传统和故事。

sentences.en: And is that why he is on a horse?
sentences.zh: 这就是他骑着马的原因吗？

sentences.en: Because that is an innovation, right?
sentences.zh: 因为那是一个创新，对吧？

sentences.en: That previously these people were never on horseback.
sentences.zh: 以前这些人从来不上马。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: And I think that this is the thing where there might be a direct link between the Greek myth and the figure of George.
sentences.zh: 我认为这就是希腊神话与乔治的形象之间可能存在直接联系的地方。

sentences.en: And it's not a narrative.
sentences.zh: 这不是一个叙事。

sentences.en: It's a kind of it's an image because the image of a saint on a horse is something that does reach back kind of to it's kind of fourth, fifth century, perhaps.
sentences.zh: 它是一种图像，因为骑马圣人的形象可以追溯到大约四、五世纪。

sentences.en: And it's something that's very popular in Egypt.
sentences.zh: 而且它在埃及非常受欢迎。

sentences.en: And you have an unnamed rider who has a halo.
sentences.zh: 你有一个头顶光环的无名骑士。

sentences.en: His spear on the bottom has a cross.
sentences.zh: 他的长矛底部有一个十字架。

sentences.en: And he is spearing a kind of supine serpent kind of lying at his feet.
sentences.zh: 他正在刺向一条躺在他脚下的仰面朝天的巨蛇。

sentences.en: And there is this inscription, the one God conquers all.
sentences.zh: 上面有这样一行铭文：独一真神征服一切。

sentences.en: And it's clear that this in turn derives from the figure of a Greek hero called Bellerophon,
sentences.zh: 很明显，这反过来又源自一个名叫柏勒洛丰的希腊英雄的形象，

sentences.en: who rides the winged horse Pegasus and spears a monster called the Chimera, which in the kind of the classical form, it's a kind of compound of a lion, a goat and a snake.
sentences.zh: 他骑着带翅膀的天马珀伽索斯，用长矛刺死了一头名为喀迈拉的怪兽，在古典形式中，它是一种狮子、山羊和蛇的结合体。

sentences.en: This is an image that goes all the way back to, you know, archaic Greece, 6th, 7th century
sentences.zh: 这个形象可以一直追溯到公元前6、7世纪的

sentences.en: BC.
sentences.zh: 古希腊时期。

sentences.en: But we know, you know, it's incredibly popular, even with Christians, because actually there's kind of a mosaic found in Dorset at Hinton St. Mary.
sentences.zh: 但我们知道，它非常受欢迎，甚至对基督徒来说也是如此，因为在多塞特的辛顿圣玛丽实际上发现了一种马赛克。

sentences.en: It's the famous one that people have probably seen.
sentences.zh: 这是人们可能都见过的那个著名的马赛克。

sentences.en: It's got a kind of beardless mosaic of Christ looking a bit like Apollo.
sentences.zh: 上面有一个胡须的基督马赛克，看起来有点像阿波罗。

sentences.en: But there's another one that's also in a kind of roundel that shows Bellerophon spearing the Chimera.
sentences.zh: 但还有另一个马赛克也在一个圆形饰带中，展示了柏勒洛丰用长矛刺死喀迈拉的场景。

sentences.en: So this idea of a man on a horse spearing a monster that is a symbol of evil, this is something that Christians seem to have been happy with.
sentences.zh: 因此，这种“骑马男子用长矛刺死象征邪恶的怪兽”的想法，似乎是基督徒们乐于接受的。

sentences.en: And I think that it generates image of a figure on horseback spearing a monster, and that this
sentences.zh: 我认为它产生了一个“骑马者用长矛刺死怪兽”的形象，

sentences.en: is why the stories of St. George killing the dragon are so instantaneously popular once he becomes associated with them.
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么一旦圣乔治与它们联系在一起，他杀死巨龙的故事就会瞬间变得如此受欢迎。

sentences.en: And although that image is specific to the Byzantine world, it's an image that emerges from the Greek half of what had been the Roman Empire.
sentences.zh: 尽管这个形象是拜占庭世界所特有的，但它诞生于曾是罗马帝国的希腊语半壁江山。

sentences.en: But you can also see why, you know, a martial figure on horseback fighting a dragon would have appealed to the knights of Latin Europe in the high Middle Ages.
sentences.zh: 但你也可以理解为什么一个骑马战斗的尚武形象在盛期中世纪会吸引拉丁欧洲的骑士。

sentences.en: Oh yeah, of course.
sentences.zh: 哦，是的，当然。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: And I think it's really telling that the cult of St. George starts to take off in Latin
sentences.zh: 我认为非常能说明问题的是，圣乔治的崇拜在11世纪的

sentences.en: Christendom in the 11th century, which is when you start getting knights emerging as
sentences.zh: 拉丁基督教世界开始兴起，正是在这个时候，骑士开始成为西方基督教世界的

sentences.en: the kind of the shock troops of Christendom in the West, and particularly the Normans, actually.
sentences.zh: 主力突击部队，尤其是诺曼人。

sentences.en: So the Normans, you know, they famously conquer England, but they're also fighting in Sicily, often against the Byzantines.
sentences.zh: 所以诺曼人，你知道，他们以征服英格兰而闻名，但他们也在西西里作战，通常是对抗拜占庭人。

sentences.en: So they may well have picked it up there.
sentences.zh: 所以他们很可能就是从那里学来的。

sentences.en: And there's an account late in the 11th century that the Normans are fighting the Saracens who
sentences.zh: 11世纪后期的一份记载称，诺曼人正在与驻扎在西西里的萨拉森人作战，

sentences.en: were based in Sicily, and St. George appears before them in shining armor, carrying a white banner decorated with a cross.
sentences.zh: 而圣乔治身穿闪亮的盔甲出现在他们面前，手持一面饰有十字架的白色旗帜。

sentences.en: So is this where the flag of St. George comes from, the famous image of the white banner with the cross?
sentences.zh: 那么，圣乔治的旗帜就是从这里来的吗？也就是那个带十字架的白色旗帜的著名形象？

sentences.en: That sounds very like the flag of St. George.
sentences.zh: 听起来非常像圣乔治的旗帜。

sentences.en: Well, is the cross red?
sentences.zh: 嗯，十字架是红色的吗？

sentences.en: That's the key thing.
sentences.zh: 这是关键所在。

sentences.en: We don't know.
sentences.zh: 我们不知道。

sentences.en: Because the Normans, of course, lots of them go on the First Crusade.
sentences.zh: 因为诺曼人，当然，他们中有很多人参加了第一次十字军东征。

sentences.en: And before the walls of Jerusalem, when they're attempting to storm the city, George is described as appearing to them again.
sentences.zh: 在耶路撒冷城墙前，当他们试图攻城时，据说乔治再次向他们显现。

sentences.en: And this time he's described as wearing white armor marked with a red cross.
sentences.zh: 这一次，据说他穿着印有红十字的白色盔甲。

sentences.en: So again, that's kind of intriguing.
sentences.zh: 所以这再次令人回味。

sentences.en: Is the red cross on a white background?
sentences.zh: 红十字是在白色背景上吗？

sentences.en: Is there something going on there with the purity of white and red being the blood of Christ or something like that?
sentences.zh: 这其中是不是有什么关于纯洁的白色和象征基督之血的红色的寓意？

sentences.en: I suppose so.
sentences.zh: 我想是的。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: And so it's often claimed that Richard the Lionheart picks up on this and that this is how it comes back to England.
sentences.zh: 因此，人们经常声称狮心王理查注意到了这一点，并将其带回了英格兰。

sentences.en: He's always shown in the flag of St. George on his tunic.
sentences.zh: 他的束腰外衣上总是显示着圣乔治的旗帜。

sentences.en: But the truth is that actually that's not true.
sentences.zh: 但事实并非如此。

sentences.en: Oh no.
sentences.zh: 哦，不。

sentences.en: Tom, don't do this.
sentences.zh: 汤姆，别这样。

sentences.en: So shockingly, in the Third Crusade, it's the French who wear red crosses and the English wear white ones.
sentences.zh: 令人震惊的是，在第三次十字军东征中，法国人戴着红十字，而英国人戴着白十字。

sentences.en: Well, some of us think the French legally should still be wearing.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我们中的一些人认为从法律上讲法国人应该继续戴着。

sentences.en: I mean, you know, if only the royal family had the decency to press their claim, the French would be wearing red crosses to this day.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，你知道的，要是王室有勇气坚持他们的主张，法国人至今仍会佩戴红十字。

sentences.en: I suppose.
sentences.zh: 我想是的。

sentences.en: But I think what that suggests is that in the 12th century, certainly there isn't a clear identification of a red cross on a white background.
sentences.zh: 但我认为这表明，在12世纪，白色背景上的红十字确实还没有得到明确的认同。

sentences.en: First of all, with Crusaders per se, and secondly, with St. George as being a kind of a figure who can be associated with England.
sentences.zh: 首先，并非专门指十字军，其次，也没有将其视为可以与英格兰联系在一起的圣乔治的标志。

sentences.en: And it's really not until the 13th century.
sentences.zh: 直到13世纪才真正如此。

sentences.en: So that is when the tradition of George fighting the dragon has been translated into Latin.
sentences.zh: 也就是在那时，乔治与巨龙搏斗的传统被翻译成了拉丁文。

sentences.en: And so it's accessible that you start to get this sense that his arms are a plain red cross on a white field.
sentences.zh: 因此人们很容易理解，并开始觉得他的纹章是白色背景上的一个素净的红十字。

sentences.en: Are we now into, let me just think about my medieval kings, we're now into the Edwards, are we?
sentences.zh: 我们现在进入……让我想想我的中世纪国王……我们现在进入爱德华时期了吗？

sentences.en: The 13th century?
sentences.zh: 13世纪？

sentences.en: We are.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So the English king who first adopts this cross, this cross of St. George, the red cross on a white background as his emblem is Edward I.
sentences.zh: 所以，第一个采用这个十字架（圣乔治十字架，即白色背景上的红十字）作为其徽章的英国国王是爱德华一世。

sentences.en: And he does it during his wars of conquest in Wales.
sentences.zh: 他在征服威尔士的战争中这样做了。

sentences.en: The dragon.
sentences.zh: 巨龙。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So Edward had been on crusade.
sentences.zh: 所以爱德华参加过十字军东征。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: So he would be familiar with this.
sentences.zh: 所以他对这个很熟悉。

sentences.en: But of course, we talked about this yesterday.
sentences.zh: 但当然，我们昨天讨论过这个。

sentences.en: The dragon is the emblem of Wales.
sentences.zh: 巨龙是威尔士的徽章。

sentences.en: And so you can see how this would have gelled very, very neatly with kind of Edward's requirements.
sentences.zh: 所以你可以看出这与爱德华的需求是如何完美契合的。

sentences.en: But as we also said at the beginning of the programme, it's actually Edward III with the
sentences.zh: 但正如我们在节目开始时也说过的那样，实际上是爱德华三世通过

sentences.en: Order of the Garter who really institutionalises the place of St. George in the English court.
sentences.zh: 嘉德勋章真正将圣乔治在英国宫廷中的地位制度化了。

sentences.en: Because up until that point, Edward I and Edward III's devotion to St. George was personal to them.
sentences.zh: 因为在此之前，爱德华一世和爱德华三世对圣乔治的崇拜是他们个人的事。

sentences.en: But what Edward III does is to say, no, we're putting this at the heart of court ritual.
sentences.zh: 但爱德华三世所做的是说，不，我们要把这一点置于宫廷礼仪的核心。

sentences.en: And you can see over the course of the 14th century that this is starting to percolate out.
